To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the serum levels of the cytoplasmatic isoenzyme of aspartate amino-transferase (AST) are higher in acute liver diseases and that the serum levels and the ratio of the mitochondrial to total AST are higher in chronic liver diseases.

the cytoplasm isoenzyme of aspartate a minotransferase (AST) is found in greater quantity than the mitochondrial isozyme, but the level increases to a greater degree in acute liver diseases, and the values of mitochondrial AST activity and the ratio to total AST in alcoholic hepatitis are greater than expected from the levels of other hepatic enzymes.

serum mitochondrial aspartate amino-transferase isoenzyme activity and the ratio between mitochondrial and total aspartate amino-transaminase are good indicators of the severity of hepato-cellular damage and that they can help to differentiate between various liver diseases, especially alcoholic hepatitis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the usefulness of serum aspartate a minotransferase determination for evaluating liver diseases.
the clinical and diagnostic significance of serum mitochondrial aspartate amino transferase.
the clinical and diagnostic significance of the measurement of aspartate aaminotransferase iso-enzymes in serum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the measurement of serum aspartate aaminotransferase isoforms can be useful in the differential diagnosis of hepatic disease and in estimating the extent and severity of hepatic injury.
the determination of aspartate aaminotransferase isoenzymes is a useful tool in the diagnosis of hepatic diseases, especially if combined with the measurement of other enzymes.

the determination of mitochondrial aspartatetransferase activity and of the ratio of the mitochondrial to total aspaate aminotrasnferase is a simple and useful method for the diagnosis and prognosis of liver disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mitochondrial enzymes are more useful than cytoplasmic enzymes for estimating the degree of hepatic damage and the type of liver disease.

the determination of serum aspartate a minotransferase and mitochondrial aspartate amino transferase activities is useful in the diagnosis of liver diseases and in evaluating the degree of hepatic injury.

mitochondrial aspartate amino-transferase activity and the activity ratio of mitochondrial to cytoplasmic aspartate amina-transferase are good markers of liver damage and that the mitochondrial enzyme is more sensitive than the cytoplasmatic one in acute hepatitis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
serum aspartate amino transferase isoenzyme measurements are useful in estimating the severity and type of liver damage.
serum mitochondrial aspartate transaminase (mAST) is a useful marker for the diagnosis of acute liver injury and the evaluation of liver function in chronic liver disease.
the determination of aspartate a minotransferase isoforms can help to clarify the clinical and diagnostic significance of liver damage.
